title: Dense bit-matrix SIMD kernels
description:
New SIMD kernels for dense bit-matrix operations. Each kernel adds a `maybe_<op>()` accessor to `gf2_core::simd` plus an unsafe AVX2 implementation in `gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/`.

## Children (3 tasks)

- **B1** — `BitMatrix::transpose` 64×64 bit-block (`crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:858-870`). Currently O(n²) bit-by-bit. PPC steps: V0 → V4 tile + bit-twiddle (Hacker's Delight ch. 7.3) → V3 SIMD via PSHUFB (8×8 byte tiles within YMM) → V7 cache layout for n>8K. Target ≥10× on n=4096.
- **B2** — M4RM Gray-code table build (`crates/gf2-core/src/alg/m4rm.rs:build_gray_table`). PPC steps: V2 ILP (8 independent table accumulators) → V3 SIMD batched XOR → V6 prefetch into table for next column block. Target measurable from existing `m4rm_profile.rs` baseline.
- **B3** — M4RM block multiply column-block scheduling (`crates/gf2-core/src/alg/m4rm.rs:multiply`). PPC steps: V4 register tile (M=8 row-acc × N=4 col-words) → V5 reuse 32-row register tile across full Gray-table pass → V6 prefetch next k-block. The tile-reuse asm path reuses the transpose primitive added in B1.

## Success criteria

Per-task: per-kernel execution protocol from epic spec doc.
